findings.claim: AC1 carried verbatim says four triggers while the contract text and GS3 carry three; research open questions Q1 (start-of-task sync before every task) and Q2 (drop after a push) are applied silently instead of recorded for the user gate.
findings.closure: The plan has a Decisions entry for research Q1 and Q2 put to the user at the gate; AC1 is amended to three triggers with a pointer to that decision (and the spec line updated), or an after-a-push trigger is added to the contract text and GS3 checks it.

findings.claim: GS5 checks only `up to date` and `diverged:` on the Local: line; the fast-forwarded form `<old>..<new>` required by AC2/AC4 is unchecked.
findings.closure: GS5 also checks the moved form `<old>..<new>` on the `- Local:` line and fails when it is removed.

findings.claim: GS6 is not implementable as a grep: literally it hits existing github.md:180,192,202,212 outside track-back step 2; the fallback reading drops --force and bare rebase that AC3 names.
findings.closure: GS6 is two exact checks passing on the GREEN text: inside the `### Keeping local in sync` section every line matching `--force|reset --hard|rebase` belongs to the one-line Never sentence; file-wide `reset --hard` and `pull --rebase` appear only in that sentence.

findings.claim: AC5 merge leg rests only on the research hook run; no git-guard fixture pins `git merge --ff-only origin/<b>`.
GS7 duplicates fixture G16.073 (git fetch origin → pass); GS ids break the G<n>.<nnn> naming.
The pinned phrases GS3/GS4 grep for are not named, so test-writer and implementer may disagree on wording.
The then-sync clauses added to track-back step 6 and pr-assets Clean up are unchecked, and must not sit after the step-6 Exception paragraph.
